correctness.rationale: For finite Artinian R the Jacobson radical J is nilpotent and reduced quotient product of fields has no nonzero nilpotent, so nilpotence exactly equals membership in J; uniform quotient coordinates are independent. For a_i=1-1/q_i, direct multiplication yields product (1-a_i^k). Largest exponential base in 1-Pk is max a_i with multiplicity, allowing exact recursive spectral recovery; the Vandermonde determinant over distinct nonzero subset-product bases proves finite initial identifiability with at most 2^s+2^t-2 terms. P1=1/Q gives number of factors <=log2 Q and bound 2Q-2. With 1 or 2 factors P2 algebraically identifies the sum and product of the field orders; independent exact 44-multiset check shows no two-factor prefix collisions and confirms the F8 vs F2^3 x F3 length-two collision broken at k=3. Finite examples do not prove the all-ring theorem.
